summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived summary of Aaron Judge's early MLB career. The Yankees drafted him in the first round of the 2013 MLB draft, and he debuted in 2016, hitting a home run in his first at bat. It focuses on his record-breaking 2017 rookie season, including All-Star and Home Run Derby honors, Yankees and MLB rookie records, and American League monthly awards.
one_line: Aaron Judge's rise from 2013 Yankees first-round pick to record-breaking 2017 rookie season with All-Star and home run records.
key_facts: The Yankees selected Aaron Judge in the first round of the 2013 MLB draft.
Aaron Judge made his MLB debut in 2016.
Aaron Judge hit a home run in his first career at bat.
Aaron Judge had a record-breaking rookie year in 2017.
Aaron Judge was named an All-Star and won the Home Run Derby.
Aaron Judge broke the Yankees' record for home runs by a rookie, besting Joe DiMaggio's 29 with 30 before the All-Star break.
Aaron Judge broke the MLB rookie record of reaching base 164 times before the All-Star break.
Aaron Judge won the American League's Rookie of the Month Awards for April, May, and June 2017.
Aaron Judge won the American League's Player of the Month Award in June 2017.
Aaron Judge set a new MLB rookie record for home runs, surpassing Mark McGwire's total of 49.
